subject: Penumbra dedicated pool — context headroom & quantization playbook
messages: Subject: Penumbra dedicated pool — context headroom & quantization playbook

Hi Anna (and Mike),

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great product and clear ML infra requirements. You mentioned wanting predictable latency for long medical-context prompts (~32k tokens) and some traffic spikes during batch inference windows for model fine-tuning/validation. To move the Dedicated sizing conversation forward I want to capture the memory headroom assumptions and what we expect from quantization across the three model variants you flagged (base, instruction-tuned, retrieval-augmented).

Quick ask: can you confirm the following by early next week?
- Typical peak concurrent sessions during clinic hours (estimate).
- Batch job window duration and largest batch size (in sequences).
- Whether KV cache persistence between requests is required for session continuity.

I’ve attached a short capacity worksheet that maps context length -> KV cache footprint for our common 32/64-bit traces, plus an initial quantization sensitivity run we can extend. I’ll loop in our capacity SME (Marissa) to convert this into a committed GPU pool proposal once you confirm the above.

Best,

Subject: Re: Penumbra dedicated pool — context headroom & quantization playbook

Jordan — thanks, and glad to recap. Quick answers below: 
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~180 concurrent users during 09:00–12:00 PT windows, falling to ~40 off-hours.
- Batch windows: two nightly windows (01:00–03:00 PT), max batch = 1,500 sequences (mostly short).
- KV cache: yes, we need per-session KV persistence for multi-turn diagnostic flows; TTL ~30 minutes is acceptable.

We are most concerned about the 32k instruction-tuned variant for latency SLAs. For procurement, Mike needs an initial committed GPU count and an SLA-backed latency target for the lead model.

Thanks — Anna

Subject: Fwd: Penumbra dedicated pool — context headroom & quantization playbook

Folks — forwarding Penumbra answers. Key constraints: 180 concurrent interactive sessions at 32k context with KV persistence (TTL 30m); two nightly batch windows up to 1.5k sequences. Procurement wants committed GPU count + SLA for the lead model (32k instruction-tuned).

Initial thoughts I captured below — please review and flag any risks before I send the proposed commit to Anna/Mike.

--- Jordan (forwarded) ---
On Sun, Jul 21, 2029 at 10:12 AM Anna Patel <anna@penumbra.ai> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks, and glad to recap. Quick answers below: 
> - Peak concurrent sessions: ~180 concurrent users during 09:00–12:00 PT windows, falling to ~40 off-hours.
> - Batch windows: two nightly windows (01:00–03:00 PT), max batch = 1,500 sequences (mostly short).
> - KV cache: yes, we need per-session KV persistence for multi-turn diagnostic flows; TTL ~30 minutes is acceptable.

Marissa / Karthik — my preliminary sizing assumptions:
- Target p95 latency for 32k model: <= 420 ms (strict) for interactive flow.
- We assume per-session average prompt+response ~8k tokens, but KV cache must support worst-case 32k context for a subset (~10% of sessions).
- Memory: instruction-tuned 32k (fp16 baseline) expected GPU mem ~40–48 GB including KV cache; with 4-bit quantization (Q4 and Q4_0), RAM drops by ~35–45% but quality/regression risk needs eval; Q8_0 gives smaller gains.

Marissa — can you run a quick pod-sizing table mapping: reserved GPU type options (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, GH200-80GB if available) -> concurrent sessions per GPU given our batching assumptions + KV persistence? Flag headroom for burst spikes and nightly batch backfill. Also include an ops recommendation on backup routing to a slightly higher-latency variant if we hit capacity.

Thanks — J.
Subject: Re: Penumbra dedicated pool — context headroom & quantization playbook (proposal attached)

Anna / Jordan / Mike — attaching a concise committed-pool proposal and the quant-sensitivity summary we ran against your sample workload. Highlights: 

1) Committed pool recommendation (production SLA, reserved):
- Proposal: 6 x H100-80GB GPUs as the committed pool. Rationale: each H100 (80 GB) supports ~35 concurrent interactive sessions at p95 <= 420ms with KV persistence for the 32k instruction-tuned variant when using fp16 baseline and our continuous batching defaults. That maps to 6*35=210 headroom for the 180-concurrent target (17% cushion).

2) Quantization strategy: 
- Short-term (safe): Q8_0 on base / retrieval variants, keep instruction-tuned at fp16 for initial rollout to avoid accuracy regressions in medical diagnostic prompts.
- Medium-term (optional optimization): run A/B with Q4_0 on a small % of traffic (5–10%) for the instruction-tuned model; if eval metrics (recall/clinical FNs) are within thresholds we can move more traffic. Our sensitivity run showed a ~38% reduction in GPU memory use for Q4_0 on the instruction-tuned weights but with marginal drop in some class-level recalls (we include the PDF with per-slice results).

3) Nightly batch window handling:
- Keep batch jobs on a separate dedicated node pool (2 x A100-40GB) that can process the 1.5k sequences without impacting interactive SLA; jobs will backfill into committed pool only if batch queue exceeds threshold for more than 15 minutes.

4) Ops / fallbacks:
- Automatic routing policy: if p95 > 420ms or GPU utilization > 85% for > 2 min, route new traffic to a slightly cheaper variant (reduced context trimming or Q8_0 variant) with a rollout knob in the Console.
- Observability: we’ll provide token-level latency and cost dashboards and a weekly quant-regression digest to monitor for drift.

Attachments: committed-pool-proposal.pdf (proposal), quant-sensitivity.pdf (per-slice results), capacity_matrix.xlsx (worksheet).

If this looks good I’ll produce a formal SOW for procurement with pricing and SLA language.

—Marissa
